mainTopic: Confession before execution, the story of עכן, and when the nation became responsible for individuals' sins
overview: This amud opens with two teachings of רבי יהושע בן לוי. Whoever conquers his יצר הרע and confesses honors הקב"ה in two worlds. A humble, broken spirit counts as every קרבן, and such a person's תפילה is not rejected. Then a new משנה teaches that about ten אמות from the place of סקילה, the condemned man is told to confess, because confession earns a share in עולם הבא, as we see with עכן. Someone who cannot confess says, 'May my death be an atonement for all my sins.' רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about whether a man framed by lying witnesses may leave out that one sin. The גמרא then expands on the story of עכן: why יהושע said 'please', how the lots found עכן, and how many times עכן had taken from חרם. This leads to a question: why was the nation not punished earlier? The answer is that the nation was not punished for hidden sins until it crossed the ירדן. רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה argue over how the dots in the פסוק 'הנסתרות לה׳ אלהינו' teach this. A new question begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Conquering your inclination and confessing honors ה׳ in two worlds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that whoever 'slaughters' his יצר הרע and confesses is credited with honoring הקב"ה in this world and in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Anyone who overpowers his evil inclination and confesses his sin is credited by the פסוק as if he honored הקב"ה in two worlds, this world and the next. The פסוק says: 'Whoever slaughters a thanks-offering honors Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a short teaching about how great it is to beat your יצר הרע and confess.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'זובח תודה' (slaughtering a thanks-offering) as 'slaughtering' your יצר and confessing (וידוי). The double letter נ in the word יכבדנני hints at honor in two worlds.

keyTerms.meaning: Inclination, here the evil inclination (יצר הרע)
The פסוק credits him as if he did something
Thanks-offering; it also sounds like וידוי (confession)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Anyone who slaughters his evil inclination
and confesses over it,
the verse credits him
as if he honored the Holy One, Blessed be He,
in two worlds:
this world and the World to Come,
as it is written: "Whoever slaughters a thanks-offering honors Me."
phrases.notes: תהלים 50:23. The word יכבדנני has two נ's, which hint at the two worlds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with an אגדה about confession. It is connected to the פסוק quoted just before on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Conquering the יצר and confessing counts as honoring הקב"ה in this world and in עולם הבא.

steps.title: A humble spirit is worth all the offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that each קרבן earns only its own reward, but a humble person is credited as if he brought every קרבן, and his תפילה is not rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי also said: When the בית המקדש stands, someone who brings an עולה gets the reward of an עולה, and someone who brings a מנחה gets the reward of a מנחה. But someone with a humble mind is credited as if he brought all the קרבנות, as it says: 'The offerings of God are a broken spirit.' And more than that, his תפילה is not rejected, as it says: 'A broken and crushed heart, God, You will not despise.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי adds a second teaching. A humble, broken spirit is worth more than any single קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each קרבן gets its own limited reward. Humility gets credit for all of them, because the פסוק says 'זבחי' (offerings, plural). The end of the same פסוק adds a second benefit: his תפילה is never turned away.
steps.whatToRemember: Humility and confession are treated as greater than קרבנות. They honor הקב"ה, count as every קרבן, and keep one's תפילה from being rejected.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
When the Temple is standing,
if a person brings a burnt-offering,
he has the reward of a burnt-offering in his hand;
a meal-offering, he has the reward of a meal-offering in his hand.
But one whose mind is humble,
the verse credits him
as if he brought all the offerings, every one of them,
as it is said: "The offerings of God are a broken spirit."
phrases.notes: תהלים 51:19. "Offerings" is plural, so a broken spirit counts as all of them.

phrases.english: And not only that, but
his prayer is not rejected,
as it is said: "A broken and crushed heart,
God, You will not despise."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same אמורא on a related theme of humility and repentance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A humble spirit is credited as all the קרבנות, and the humble person's תפילה is not rejected.

steps.title: The condemned man is told to confess, as עכן did
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that about ten אמות from the place of סקילה the condemned man is told to confess, because confession earns a share in עולם הבא, as we see with עכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: When he was about ten אמות from the place of stoning, they tell him, 'Confess,' because all who are executed confess. Whoever confesses has a share in עולם הבא. We see this with עכן: יהושע told him, 'My son, please give glory to ה׳, God of Israel, and confess to Him,' and עכן answered, 'Truly, I have sinned, and I did such and such.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes the confession the condemned man makes just before his execution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the practical rule: confess about ten אמות before the place of stoning. It also gives the reason: confession earns עולם הבא. It brings the story of עכן as the model of a condemned man who confessed.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who took from the forbidden spoils of יריחו

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of saying וידוי before death. Even a person sentenced by בית דין can earn עולם הבא through confession.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: When he was distant from the place of stoning
about ten cubits,
they say to him: "Confess,"
for such is the way of all who are executed: they confess.
For whoever confesses
has a share in the World to Come,
for so we find with Achan,
that Joshua said to him:
"My son, please give glory

phrases.aramaic: לַה׳ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְתֶן לוֹ תוֹדָה״.
phrases.english: to the Lord, God of Israel, and make confession to Him."
"And Achan answered Joshua
and said: Truly, I have sinned
and like this and like this, etc."
phrases.notes: יהושע 7:20. The "etc." means the פסוק goes on to describe exactly what he did.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָיָה רָחוֹק מִבֵּית הַסְּקִילָה כְּעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It returns to the order of the execution procedure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: About ten אמות from the place of stoning, the condemned man is told to confess, because confession earns a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Proof that עכן's confession atoned for him
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how we know עכן's confession worked. It proves it from יהושע's words 'on this day', which limit his trouble to this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know his confession atoned for him? The פסוק says: 'And יהושע said: Why have you troubled us? ה׳ will trouble you on this day.' This means: on this day you are troubled, but you will not be troubled in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up its claim. It shows from a פסוק that עכן's confession really earned him atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we only saw that עכן confessed, not that it helped him. The extra words 'ביום הזה' (on this day) show that his punishment stops with this world. So his confession saved him in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where (do we learn this)?

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the wordplay: עכן's name and the word עכר (to trouble) sound alike. The proof itself rests on the limiting words 'ביום הזה', meaning only today.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that his confession atoned for him?
As it is said: "And Joshua said:
Why have you troubled us?
The Lord shall trouble you on this day."
On this day you are troubled,
but you are not troubled in the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the משנה's claim from step 3 that confession earns עולם הבא.
steps.raayaObject: That confession before execution atones and secures עולם הבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 7:25, 'יעכרך ה׳ ביום הזה', which limits the trouble to this day only

steps.title: A simple formula for someone who cannot confess
steps.stepSummary: If the condemned man does not know how to confess, they give him a simple line to say: 'May my death be an atonement for all my sins.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he does not know how to confess, they tell him: Say, 'May my death be an atonement for all my sins.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with a man who cannot put together a confession. It gives him a short, ready-made sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Confession does not need detailed words. A simple request that his death atone for everything is enough. This is the תנא קמא's position, which the next step will argue with.

phrases.english: And if he does not know how to confess,
they say to him: Say:
"May my death be an atonement
for all my sins."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the confession rule to a man who cannot confess on his own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who cannot confess says: 'May my death be an atonement for all my sins.'

steps.title: רבי יהודה: an innocent man may leave out the sin he did not commit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the condemned man knows he was convicted by lying witnesses, he adds 'except for this sin' to his confession.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If he knows that he was convicted by false (זוממין) witnesses, he says, 'May my death be an atonement for all my sins except this sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds an exception for an innocent man who was framed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An innocent man should not be forced to admit to a sin he never did. So רבי יהודה lets him leave out the crime he was convicted of, while still asking atonement for everything else.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he knew that he was convicted by lying witnesses,
he says: "May my death be an atonement

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל עֲוֹנוֹתַי חוּץ מֵעָוֹן זֶה״.
phrases.english: for all my sins except for this sin."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהוּא מְזוּמָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the standard formula from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who knows he was falsely convicted adds 'except for this sin' to his confession.

steps.title: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's exception
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה that if this were allowed, every condemned man would say it to clear his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If so, everyone will say this in order to clear themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against רבי יהודה's exception with a practical problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the formula included 'except this sin', every condemned man, guilty or not, would use it to look innocent. That would make בית דין's verdict look doubtful in the public eye. So the חכמים do not offer this wording.
steps.whatToRemember: The confession formula is simple and covers all sins. רבי יהודה lets a framed man leave out the false charge, but the חכמים reject this because everyone would then use it to clear his name.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, יְהוּ כׇּל אָדָם אוֹמְרִין כֵּן
phrases.english: If so, every person will say that
in order to clear themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's exception from step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יהודה's proposed 'except for this sin' formula
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Everyone, guilty or innocent, would use it to clear his name, which would make the court's verdict look doubtful.

steps.title: The word 'נא' means please
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא notes that יהושע's word 'נא' to עכן is a word of asking, not ordering.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'נא' always means asking, like 'please'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא about the פסוק the משנה used for עכן. It points out that יהושע spoke to עכן with the word 'please'. This sets up the next question: why would יהושע beg a sinner?
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע was the leader and judge, so he could simply order עכן to confess. Saying 'please' is surprising. The next steps explain why יהושע needed עכן's cooperation.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this opens a ברייתא
A way of speaking that asks

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
"Na": "na" is nothing but an expression of request.
phrases.notes: This is from יהושע ז:יט, where יהושע tells עכן 'שים נא כבוד', 'please give honor'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״נָא״ – אֵין ״נָא״ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן בַּקָּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by expanding on the עכן story the משנה quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע's word 'נא' shows that he was asking עכן, not ordering him.

steps.title: The lots fall on עכן, and he challenges them
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ would not name the sinner and told יהושע to cast lots. The lot fell on עכן, who argued that a lot proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ה׳ told יהושע 'Israel sinned', יהושע asked who it was. ה׳ answered, 'Am I a snitch? Go cast lots.' יהושע did, and the lot fell on עכן. עכן said: 'You come against me with a lot? You and אלעזר הכהן are the two greatest people of the generation. If I cast a lot between the two of you, it will land on one of you!'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells the background story. It explains why יהושע had to say 'please' to עכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גורל always lands on someone, even if that person is innocent. That was עכן's argument. His challenge put the trustworthiness of the גורל itself in danger, and this sets up יהושע's reply.

keyTerms.meaning: A lot, a lottery used to pick out someone
The man who took forbidden spoils from יריחו
The great leaders of the generation

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: At the time that the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Yehoshua:
"Israel has sinned,"

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, מִי חָטָא?
phrases.english: he said before Him: Master of the World, who sinned?
He said to him: Am I an informer?
Go cast lots.
He went and cast lots,
and the lot fell on Achan.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, בְּגוֹרָל אַתָּה בָּא עָלַי?
phrases.english: He said to him: Yehoshua, you come against me with a lot?
You and Elazar the Kohen
are the two greatest of the generation.
If I cast a lot on you,
it will fall on one of you.
phrases.notes: He means that a lot has to land on somebody, so it does not prove that person did anything wrong.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the background that explains why יהושע used 'נא'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lot found עכן, but עכן argued that a lot cannot prove guilt.

steps.title: יהושע begs עכן not to discredit the lots
steps.stepSummary: יהושע pleads with עכן not to cast doubt on the גורל, because ארץ ישראל will one day be divided by גורל.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהושע said to him: 'I beg you, don't speak badly about the lots. ארץ ישראל is going to be divided by lot, as the פסוק says, "Only by lot shall the land be divided."'
steps.whatsHappening: Here we get the answer to why יהושע said 'please'. He needed עכן to confess so that people would keep trusting the גורל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If עכן denied his guilt, people might say the גורל can be wrong. Then the later division of ארץ ישראל by גורל could be questioned. So יהושע was not asking for himself. He was protecting the גורל.
steps.whatToRemember: יהושע said 'נא' to עכן because he needed עכן's confession to protect the trust in the גורל that would divide ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: He said to him: I ask of you,
do not spread slander about the lots,
since Eretz Yisrael is destined to be divided by lot,
as it is said: "Only by lot shall the land be divided."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּבַקָּשָׁה מִמְּךָ, אַל תּוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל הַגּוֹרָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עכן's challenge and finishes explaining the word 'נא'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יהושע asked politely because he needed עכן's confession to protect the trust in the גורל used to divide ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: יהושע wins עכן over, and he confesses
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that יהושע persuaded עכן with gentle words, and עכן confessed right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Make confession.' רבינא said: יהושע won him over with words: 'All we want from you is a confession. Confess to Him and be free.' Right away, 'עכן answered יהושע and said: Truly I have sinned to ה׳, God of Israel, and like this and like this I have done.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the same פסוק, 'make confession'. רבינא explains how יהושע got עכן to admit his sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע made confessing sound easy: 'just confess and be free'. That gentle talk worked, and עכן confessed at once. His words 'like this and like this' prepare the next discussion about how many times he sinned.

keyTerms.meaning: He 'bribed' him; he won him over
And be free, be done with it

phrases.english: "Make confession."
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק, יהושע ז:יט.

phrases.english: Ravina said: He won him over with words:
Do we ask anything of you but a confession?
Make confession to Him and be free.
Immediately: "And Achan answered Yehoshua and said:

phrases.aramaic: אׇמְנָה אָנֹכִי חָטָאתִי לַה׳ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: Truly I have sinned against ה׳, God of Israel,
and like this and like this I have done."

steps.triggerLanguage: ״תֵּן תּוֹדָה״. אָמַר רָבִינָא, שַׁחוֹדֵי שַׁחֲדֵיהּ בְּמִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the פסוק and shows how יהושע got the confession.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע got עכן to confess by speaking gently and making confession sound simple.

steps.title: עכן misused three sets of dedicated spoils
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא learns from 'כזאת וכזאת' that עכן had taken חרם three times: twice in the days of משה and once in the days of יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said in the name of רבי חנינא: This teaches that עכן misused three sets of חרם, two in the days of משה and one in the days of יהושע, as it says, 'like this and like this I have done.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why עכן's confession repeats 'like this and like this'. רבי חנינא says it shows that עכן had sinned before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'כזאת' hints at an earlier sin from the days of משה. Adding the sin at יריחו, in the days of יהושע, makes three in total.

keyTerms.meaning: Spoils set aside as holy and forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
This teaches that Achan misused three sets of dedicated spoils,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנַיִם בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה וְאֶחָד בִּימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: two in the days of Moshe and one in the days of Yehoshua,
as it is said: "Like this and like this I have done."
phrases.notes: He reads each 'כזאת' as one earlier time. Those two times plus יריחו make three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁמָּעַל עָכָן בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה חֲרָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words 'כזאת וכזאת' from the confession just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עכן misused חרם three times: twice under משה and once under יהושע.

steps.title: A second view: עכן sinned five times
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, says עכן misused חרם five times: four under משה and one under יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: Five times, four in the days of משה and one in the days of יהושע, as it says, 'I have sinned, and like this and like this I have done.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion reads the same confession differently. It counts five sins instead of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opinion includes more words from the פסוק, starting with 'אנכי חטאתי'. It finds more hints of earlier sins. Both opinions agree that only one sin happened under יהושע. They argue only about how many happened under משה.
steps.whatToRemember: עכן's 'like this and like this' shows that he had sinned before. One opinion says three times in total, the other says five.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשָּׁה, אַרְבָּעָה בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה וְאֶחָד בִּימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: Five: four in the days of Moshe and one in the days of Yehoshua,
as it is said: "I have sinned, and like this and like this I have done."
phrases.notes: He includes more words of the פסוק, so he finds more hints of earlier sins than רבי חנינא did.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: חֲמִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי חנינא's count by reading more of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עכן misused חרם five times: four under משה and one under יהושע.

steps.title: Why was the nation not punished earlier for עכן's sins?
steps.stepSummary: עכן had already taken from חרם back in משה's time, so why was the nation punished only now?
steps.simpleTranslation: If עכן stole even in the days of משה, why were the Jewish people not punished until now?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that comes straight out of the last two steps. If עכן sinned under משה, why did the punishment only come at עי, in יהושע's time?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12 and 13 taught that עכן took from חרם several times, some of them under משה. Until now we would have expected the nation to suffer for each time. The fact that nothing happened until now needs an explanation.

phrases.english: And until now,
what is the reason they were not punished?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the Jewish people as a whole, who were punished at עי because of עכן.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד הַשְׁתָּא, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אִיעֲנוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a problem raised by the earlier steps, which said עכן sinned under משה as well.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the nation was not punished for עכן's earlier thefts in משה's time.

steps.title: No punishment for hidden sins until crossing the ירדן
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ did not punish the nation for the hidden sins of individuals until they crossed the ירדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון‎: ה׳ did not punish the nation for hidden sins until they crossed the ירדן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. Before crossing the ירדן, the nation was not held responsible for one person's secret sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עכן's earlier thefts under משה happened before the crossing, so the nation was not responsible for them. Once they crossed into ארץ ישראל, that changed. This is why the punishment came only at עי.

keyTerms.meaning: hidden things, meaning secret sins done by individuals

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:
Because He did not punish for hidden sins
until Israel crossed the Jordan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Before the crossing of the ירדן, the nation was not punished for the hidden sins of individuals.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns the same idea from dots in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The answer matches the view of רבי יהודה, who learns it from the dots over certain words in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים. The פסוק says: 'The hidden things belong to ה׳ our God, and the revealed things belong to us and our children forever.' Why are there dots over 'to us and to our children' and over the ע of 'עד'? This teaches that ה׳ did not punish for hidden sins until Israel crossed the ירדן. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the answer from step 15 is really one side of an older dispute between תנאים. רבי יהודה learns the same idea from special dots in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dots over 'to us and to our children forever' weaken those words, as if they were partly erased. רבי יהודה reads this to mean that at first the nation was not punished for hidden sins. That changed only after the crossing of the ירדן, which is the same answer given in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: this is like a dispute between תנאים
dotted, meaning marked with dots over the letters
revealed things, meaning sins done in the open

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of Tannaim:
"The hidden things belong to ה׳ our God,
and the revealed things belong to us and to our children forever."
Why are there dots over "to us and to our children"
phrases.notes: In a ספר תורה, small dots are written above the letters of these words.

phrases.english: and over the letter ayin in "until/forever"?
It teaches that He did not punish for hidden sins
until Israel crossed the Jordan,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer of step 15 matches רבי יהודה's side of a dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the dots show that the nation was not punished for hidden sins until after the crossing of the ירדן.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: the nation is never punished for hidden sins
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה challenges רבי יהודה: the פסוק says hidden sins belong to ה׳ forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said to him: Does ה׳ ever punish the nation for hidden sins? The פסוק already says 'forever'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה attacks רבי יהודה's reading. He says the nation is never punished for secret sins, not even after the ירדן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's view suggests that after the crossing, the nation is punished for hidden sins. רבי נחמיה says this cannot be. The פסוק gives hidden sins to ה׳ 'forever', so the nation is never responsible for them.

keyTerms.meaning: and is it so that...? (a question showing surprise)

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said to him:
And does He ever punish for hidden sins?
But it is already stated "forever"!
phrases.notes: He reads 'forever' as part of 'the hidden things belong to ה׳': they stay with ה׳ forever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's reading of the dots from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that the nation was punished for hidden sins after the crossing of the ירדן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'עד עולם' show that hidden sins belong to ה׳ forever. So the nation is never punished for them, either before or after the ירדן.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: the dots refer to sins done in the open
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says the dots teach that before the ירדן, the nation was not even punished for open sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, just as ה׳ never punished the nation for hidden sins, so too He did not punish the nation for sins done in the open until Israel crossed the ירדן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה gives his own explanation of the dots. They are not about hidden sins, which are never punished. They are about sins done in the open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נחמיה, hidden sins never bring punishment on the nation. The dots over 'to us and our children' weaken only the part about revealed sins. That part did not apply until after the ירדן.

keyTerms.meaning: that are done in the open
punishable sins, sins that bring punishment

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: before the ירדן, the nation was not punished for hidden sins, but after it, it was. רבי נחמיה: the nation is never punished for hidden sins, and before the ירדן it was not even punished for open sins.
steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים agree that something changed at the ירדן. They only argue about what changed: hidden sins (רבי יהודה) or open sins (רבי נחמיה).

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁלֹּא עָנַשׁ עַל הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת,
phrases.english: Rather, just as He did not punish for hidden sins,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ לֹא עָנַשׁ עַל עוֹנָשִׁין שֶׁבַּגָּלוּי
phrases.english: so He did not punish for sins that are done in the open
until Israel crossed the Jordan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁלֹּא עָנַשׁ עַל הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי יהודה's reading, רבי נחמיה gives his own reading of the dots.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hidden sins are never punished on the nation. Before the ירדן, even open sins were not punished on the nation.

steps.title: Opening a new question
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אלא' begins a new question that continues right after this.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word is setting up the next move. The גמרא is starting a new question based on what we just learned, and the rest of the question comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אלא' here means 'but if so'. The גמרא is about to ask what follows from the views just stated about the ירדן. For now, simply know that a challenge is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so (here it opens a new question)

phrases.english: But if so...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The question continues right after this word.
